issue.title: chip_runtime HookResult loses exception type on subprocess failures
issue.actual_behavior: In chip_runtime.py around line 274, the except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) handler converts the exception to a string via str(exc) when building the HookResult: result={"error": str(exc)}. This loses the exception type. A TimeoutExpired produces a message like "Command '...' timed out after 30 seconds" and an OSError produces "Permission denied: ...", but callers only see the string and cannot programmatically distinguish a timeout from a filesystem permission error. This matters for retry logic, alerting, and diagnostics.
issue.expected_behavior: The HookResult for subprocess failures should include the exception class name so callers can branch on failure kind without parsing human-readable error strings. result should contain both error (the message) and error_type (the class name), e.g. {"error": "...", "error_type": "TimeoutExpired"}.
repro_steps: Open src/chip_labs/intelligence_serving/chip_runtime.py and find the except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) block around line 269-277.
Note that result={"error": str(exc)} is the only error payload — no exception type is included.
A caller receiving this HookResult sees {"error": "Command 'foo' timed out after 30 seconds"} but cannot tell if it was a TimeoutExpired or an OSError without regex parsing.
The intelligence_fallback handler (line 354-362) has the same pattern — this fix targets only the subprocess handler per scope.
issue.affected_workflow: Subprocess hook error handling — callers cannot distinguish timeout errors from filesystem permission errors, breaking retry logic and error classification

evidence.before_after_proof: Before (line 274): result={"error": str(exc)}, → {"error": "Command 'run_chip.sh' timed out after 30 seconds"} — no type info. After (line 274): result={"error": str(exc), "error_type": type(exc).__name__}, → {"error": "Command 'run_chip.sh' timed out after 30 seconds", "error_type": "TimeoutExpired"} — callers can branch on error_type.

proposed_fix.approach: Add error_type field to the HookResult result dict in the subprocess exception handler (line 274). Change result={"error": str(exc)} to result={"error": str(exc), "error_type": type(exc).__name__}. This preserves the exception class name so callers can programmatically distinguish TimeoutExpired from OSError without parsing error message strings.
proposed_fix.tests_or_smoke: Existing tests pass unchanged. The fix adds one key to an existing dict literal on the error path. No function signatures, control flow, or return types are modified. type(exc).__name__ is a safe standard Python idiom requiring no imports.

review_claim.duplicate_notes: No existing PR addresses the subprocess HookResult error_type loss in chip_runtime.py. This is a targeted single-line change in the subprocess execution path only.
review_claim.risk_notes: Minimal risk. One dict key added to an error-path-only code path. No happy-path behavior changes. No new dependencies. type(exc).__name__ is a standard Python idiom that works for all exception types.
